purpose: prioritise ONE first tactical family for Tactical Frontier Sprint 1; a research prioritisation tool, not evidence that any tactic works

anchors.5: the capability exists in at least 90% of the 50 historical scenarios and for most operator archetypes

L.name: expected tactical leverage (prior judgement, stated with its reasons)

anchors.5: can change the combat power or objective control of the whole force in most games
anchors.4: changes the effective force of most operators, with known offsetting costs
anchors.3: a local advantage for a subset of operators or situations

anchors.5: decided entirely from the seat's own observation and legal actions, cheap to compute
anchors.4: own observation plus simple bookkeeping of what was seen
anchors.3: needs an estimate or belief over partially observed enemies
anchors.2: needs a model of hidden enemy behaviour
anchors.1: needs information the seat does not have

anchors.5: one decision point outside the existing play-stage selection (for example only the deployment stage, or only operators baseline-v2 leaves idle)
anchors.4: one new behaviour for one archetype, existing selection untouched
anchors.3: changes play-stage selection for a subset of operators
anchors.2: changes shared machinery (routing, ordering, the gate)

anchors.5: the mechanism is visible directly in game records (action counts, engine acceptance, unit counts)
anchors.4: visible with existing records plus refusal facts
anchors.2: needs a new observer and a model to interpret

R.name: engineering and rule risk, reversed (safer is higher)

anchors.5: action documented and listed in valid_actions on engine 4.1.0, simple parameters, no new rule interaction
anchors.3: documented; legality or effect not visible in 4.1.0 valid_actions, or new rule interactions
anchors.2: rarely listed on 4.1.0 or complex parameters with unknown effects

P.name: historical opportunity in the frozen experimental population

anchors.5: applicable in every frozen scenario side and every game
anchors.4: at least 75% of frozen scenario sides

families.T1: deployment disaggregation and initial formation (actions 314 and 14; stack)
families.T2: transport, dismount and infantry objective defence (actions 3, 4, 303, 304; passengers; concealment)
families.T3: reconnaissance and enemy belief (visible-enemy history, observe_distance, UAV, loitering munitions)
families.T4: indirect artillery fire (action 8; jm_points; weapon state and cooldown)
families.T5: guided fire and correction (actions 9 and 17; guide_ability)
families.T6: threat-aware movement (routing cost with visible and last-seen enemy threat)
families.T7: movement-state micro (actions 6, 10, 11, 12: march, charge, conceal, stop, weapon lock and unfold)
families.T8: specialised assets (mines, fortifications, altitude, air defence, helicopters)
families.T9: intent and task allocation (attack, defend, reconnaissance roles; objective assignment)

selection_rule: the family with the highest weighted score is selected; ties are broken by L, then by R
scores are integers 0 to 5 per the anchors, each with a one-line reason citing the census where it applies
the weights above are fixed by this commit and are not changed after scoring
sensitivity: each weight raised and lowered by 0.05 in turn, the others rescaled to keep the sum at 1
each criterion left out in turn, the others rescaled
reported: whether the selected family stays first in each variant, and the variants in which it does not
